subject: Post-call: Audit logs & PII handling - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fincobank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Audit logs & PII handling - next steps

Hi Liam -

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

- Scope we discussed: audit logs (who accessed what/when), retention window options, export formats for evidence requests, and data residency guarantees for EU workloads.
- Immediate asks from your team: sample audit export (redacted), confirmation of which fields are included in access logs (user id, role, action, resource id, timestamp, IP), and a short note on how PII in model inputs is treated during retention/export.
- Deliverables we propose to send by end of week: redwood-audit-logs-sample.csv (redacted), JSON schema for exports, SOC2 summary, and a draft Data Processing Addendum.

Action items:
1) Liam: confirm the minimal fields you need in the export (CSV vs JSON preference) and any retention window you need us to demonstrate (e.g., 30/90/365 days).
2) Redwood (Ben + Dev): prepare a redacted sample export and a doc describing how we record access events and how PII is handled/retained.
3) Marissa: coordinate legal/DP and share HubSpot deal and secure links.

Attachments: redwood-audit-logs-spec.pdf, soc2-summary.pdf (stubs attached).

If helpful I can schedule a short follow-up next week (20-30 minutes) with Ben from security to walk through the sample.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

--
Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fincobank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Kumar <sara.kumar@fincobank.com>, procurement@fincobank.com
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Audit logs & PII handling - next steps

Thanks Marissa -

That summary is helpful. A few clarifications from our side so we can scope the evidence request properly:

- Preferred formats: CSV sample and JSON schema would be ideal. We will need at least one weekly export that we can ingest into our SIEM for verification.
- Fields: please include actor identifier (redacted is ok), actor role, action (e.g., generate, view, export), resource id, timestamp (ISO8601), source IP, and whether the payload included any PII flags.
- Retention: we need to confirm retention windows you support - target 365 days for audit logs for the initial proof.
- Residency: for EU regulated data we need assurance that logs and any persisted inputs stay in the EU region. If Redwood provides region-specific exports, please note that.
- DPA: we will require a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and may need a security questionnaire after we review the samples.

Can you include a redacted sample export and a short note describing how PII in model inputs is flagged/handled in logs? Also please provide a named security contact for follow-up.

Regards,
Liam O'Connor
Head of IT Risk | FinCo Bank
liam.oconnor@fincobank.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Audit logs & PII handling - next steps

Marissa - looping in the plan for deliverables. Below is what I can put together by Friday EOD:

1) Redacted audit logs sample (.csv) - we'll remove any identifiable customer data but preserve field structure (actor_id_redacted, actor_role, action, resource_id, timestamp, source_ip, pii_flag). Small sample (10-50 rows) suitable for ingestion.
2) JSON schema describing export format and field definitions.
3) Short note on PII handling: our ingestion pipeline flags inputs with PII using token classification heuristics; flagged inputs are marked in logs via pii_flag and are subject to configurable retention rules. We do not persist raw model inputs beyond configured retention and provide export hooks on request.
4) Region/residency note: for EU-region workloads, logs and stored inputs remain in the EU region and exports are generated from that region.
5) SOC2 summary and a draft DPA (data-processing-addendum-draft.pdf) for legal review.

Attachments I will prepare: redwood-audit-logs-sample.csv (redacted, CSV, ~12KB), redwood-audit-logs-schema.json (schema stub), data-processing-addendum-draft.pdf, soc2-summary.pdf. Once I have the redacted sample I'll upload to a secure link and share it with Liam.

Marissa - can you confirm whether FinCo prefers CSV or JSON first? Also, do we need IP subnet obfuscation beyond redaction?

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Security & Success | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fincobank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 11:47:00 -07:00

Liam -

Thanks - we can start with CSV but will include the JSON schema as well. Ben is preparing the redacted sample and the DPA draft; I expect to share the secure link with the artifacts by Friday.

For visibility, I'm including the planned deliverables again:
- redwood-audit-logs-sample.csv (redacted sample, CSV)
- redwood-audit-logs-schema.json (field definitions and types)
- soc2-summary.pdf (what we can share publicly)
- data-processing-addendum-draft.pdf (for your legal)

Secure download link (expires in 7 days): https://redwood.sharefile.com/s/secure/audit-logs-sample
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-7890

Next steps: please confirm a recipient for the artifacts (security@fincobank.com or your address) and whether FinCo needs IP obfuscation beyond redaction. Once you confirm I'll route the artifacts and loop in legal for the DPA signature.
